Resetting the Scores of all Coverable Objects to Zero
You can reset the scores of all coverable objects to zero. The scores of code, assert,
and covergroup coverage can be reset to zero. As the reset database contains the latest
covergroup shape, it can be used as a reference database to generate a report from
a union-merged database. For more information about reference database and union
merged databases, see Section Reference Merging for Covergroups and Assertions and
Union Merging for Covergroups.
Consider a scenario in which you are required to gather coverage data for eight weeks
and create merged VDBs for various time-window options. Therefore, at any given time
you can see the accumulated coverage data of the past 2 days or 4 days or 1 week
or 4 weeks, and so on. If you want to see old coverage data (for example, merged
data of the last two weeks, excluding the latest) through a newer coverage shape (the
coverage shape derived from the latest coverage data), and you need to merge the
existing set of databases against the new coverage shape. You can achieve this using the
reset database. In the reset database, the coverage data is reset to zero and the latest
coverage shape is retained.
To reset all the coverage metrics to zero, use the
-reset_coverage
-reset_coverage option along with
-dbname reset.vdb on the urg command line.
% urg -dir simv1.vdb -dir simv2.vdb …. -reset_coverage\ -dbname reset.vdb
This command enables you to dump the merged coverage database reset.vdb which
contains the scores of all coverable objects that are reset to zero. So, when you generate
the reports out of reset.vdb, the scores of each coverable object are reported as zero.

Union Merge of Modules
However, this command does not generate urgReports and therefore, -report <path
to urg reports> is ignored by URG.
It is mandatory to pass -dbname reset.vdb along with -reset_coverage.
The -show tests option is not honored if passed along with -reset_coverage.
Therefore, the dumped database does not contain any test correlation data (as no objects
are covered in the reset database, URG does not have any test to attach). However, URG
does not issue any warning for this scenario.
Union Merge of Modules
Merging combines coverage from multiple databases to produce a unified database that
contains their combined results. VCS reports coverage for each instance of each module.
It also reports merged coverage for all instances of each module that have the same
shape (that is, for each variant of the module).
If all of the databases are created from the same version of the design, each module
and instance have the same shape and the coverage is merged. While merging code
coverage across multiple configurations of the design, the objects and instances in the
base configuration are used as a reference. By default, the data for an instance in an
input database that does not exist in the base database is ignored, and its contribution to
the overall coverage score of its module is lost. In previous VCS versions, it was already
possible to collect the coverage for a specific list of modules across different design
configurations using the -map and -mapfile options. However, -map and -mapfile cannot
handle the scenario where there is no VDB containing the superset of all modules that
is used as the base VDB. The new -flex_merge modules option to URG provides the
ability to merge modules even if there is no single VDB that contains all modules. When
this option is given, URG automatically merges the code coverage for each variant of
each module that appears in any of the specified databases. The instance-level coverage
data is still reported separately, but the module-level coverage data takes data from all
configurations.
Note that module-level data is only merged when the module's coverage shape is the
same (that is, they are from the same variant of the module). For example, the data for all
instances of a 16-bit adder across different design configurations is merged together, but
the data for any 32-bit versions of the same adder is kept separate.

The -flex_merge modules option supports merging of only compile-time databases and

Union Merge of Modules
using the vcs command. For example, to create the compile-time database, simv1.vdb,
use the following command:
vcs -cm line+cond toptb -o simv1
To create a merged database, namely merged.vdb, of a compile-time database and
simulation databases, use -dbname to URG as follows:
urg -dir <compile.vdb> <sim1.vdb> <sim2.vdb> … -dbname merged.vdb
To merge simv1.vdb and merged.vdb, use -flex_merge modules as follows:
urg -dir simv1.vdb merged.vdb -flex_merge modules
If there are two separate databases for compile and simulation, pass both the databases
with -flex_merge modules as follows:
urg -dir <compile.vdb> <sim.vdb> -flex_merge modules
You should not pass simulation-only databases that contain no design hierarchy
information with -flex_merge modules . As simulation-only databases do not have
enough information for flexible module merging, URG gives the following error:
Error-[UCAPI-NCDVDB] Directory has no design information
The directory "sim.vdb" does not contain any design hierarchy information
and therefore cannot be used with -flex_merge modules.
If there is a single database for compile and simulation, pass the database of both base
and input configurations with -flex_merge modules for merging. Consider a scenario in
which simv.vdb contains compile and simulation information. To merge simv.vdb of base
and input configurations, use the following command:
urg -dir base/simv.vdb input/simv.vdb -flex_merge modules
Unlike in the default mode, the order of databases passed to URG does not change
their scores when using -flex_merge modules with the design configurations that are
different. For example, the following commands result in identical scores:
urg -dir simv1.vdb simv2.vdb -flex_merge modules -report urgReport1
urg -dir simv2.vdb simv1.vdb -flex_merge modules -report urgReport2
This feature has the following limitations:
• Test grading cannot be done when creating a report using -flex_merge modules .
You can create a merged VDB using -flex_merge modules and run test grading on it.
However, test grading works on the design hierarchy, not the modules, so each design
hierarchy (configuration) is treated as an independent set of coverable objects for test
grading.

• Modules in different libraries are treated as different entities and therefore, they are not
merged across design hierarchies.
• If a design is compiled with -cm_seqnoconst or -cm_noconst, coverable objects (such
as line, condition, branch, and toggle coverage targets) that are not reachable in that
configuration are marked unreachable. After -flex_merge modules , an object is
reported as UNREACHABLE only if it is marked unreachable in all the input VDBs.
If the object is reachable in at least one input VDB, it is reported as reachable in the
merged result.
The scoped merging feature enables a new type of VDB directory called a VDB Merged
Directory (VDM), where the design and testbench coverage from different VDBs is kept
strictly separate. A report generated from a VDM directory shows separate hierarchies and
separate sets of function coverage data for each design version.
Unlike regular merging where coverage from different VDBs is combined by name and
shape into a single unified result, scoped merging preserves the identity of each design
version. The VDBs of the original versions exist side-by-side in the result, each identified
by a unique scope name prefix.
A VDM can have additional design versions added to it incrementally. Each version in
the VDM has a unique name prefix used to distinguish it in reports and in Verdi coverage
sessions. These names can also be used to refer to different versions from inside an HVP
Verification Plan.

Command Line Usage
To create a VDM with URG, use the -flex_merge separate option. In this mode,
specify the scope name to use for each design version using the ## syntax after the
corresponding VDB name:
% urg -dir version1.vdb##v1 version2.vdb##v2 \
-dbname sepmerge12 -flex_merge separate
Additional VDBs can be added to an existing VDM:
% urg -dir sepmerge12.vdb version3.vdb##v3 \
-dbname sepmerge123 -flex_merge separate
The VDBs passed to -dir must be merged VDBs containing a single test only. Each VDB
passed to -dir must have a unique scope name specified using the ## syntax.
If a scope name is not provided, the following error is issued:
% urg -dir version1.vdb version2.vdb \
-dbname sepmerge12 -flex_merge separate

Error-[UCAPI-MSTN] Missing top name for separated merge
VDB version1.vdb was passed to -dir in flex_merge separate mode
without a top name specified.
In flex_merge separate mode a unique top name must be given for
each VDB. For example: urg -dir simv.vdb##v1
If only one VDB is passed to -dir, a new VDB is created with the specified scope name
added:
% urg -dir version4.vdb##v4 -dbname sepmerge4 -flex_merge separate
Two VDMs with unique scope names can be combined:
% urg -dir sepmerge12.vdb sepmerge34.vdb \
-dbname sepmerge1234 -flex_merge separate

The -flex_merge separate option must be specified if any input VDB is a
VDM.
Two VDMs can only be combined if all their scope names are unique. If duplicate scope
names are detected, the following error is issued:
% urg -dir sepmerge12.vdb sepmerge13.vdb \
-dbname sepmerge123 -flex_merge separate

Error-[UCAPI-SMX] Duplicate top names in separated merge
The VDMs sepmerge12.vdb and sepmerge13.vdb both contain data
with top name "v2". VDMs can only be combined when all top
names are unique.
Merging Restrictions
Any type of merged VDB may be merged as a separate VDB using -flex_merge
separate, regardless of whether it was created with default merging, -map/-mapfile, or
one of the other -flex_merge options.
However, once a VDB is merged into a VDM, its coverage can no longer be merged with
any other VDBs in any way, except to add more VDBs in other scope names to the VDM
itself. This includes any kind of default, -flex_merge, or -map/-mapfile type operation.
The VDM is intended as the last step to take before generating a report. If more data must
be added to a VDB that is going to be reported from a VDM, all of the new data should be
merged with the regular VDB first, and then a new VDM should be created.
Exclusions
Exclusions created using a VDM include scope names. As a result, those exclude files
cannot be later used on a regular VDB as it will not contain the scope name.
For example, an instance dut.chk1 under a scope name V1 would have an .el file entry
like this:
CHECKSUM: "1017343997 2493925923"
INSTANCE: ##v1.dut.chk1
Similarly, hier files specified at report time must include scope names (or wildcards) to
be used on a VDM. For example, a -hier file entry for the above instance could use this
syntax:
-tree ##v1.dut.chk1
To make entries scope-name neutral, use a wildcard:
-tree *dut.chk1

This does not apply to compile-time hier files (-cm_hier, -cm_assert_hier)
because separated scope names can only exist in a VDB, not in any design.
Reporting
When a VDM is passed to URG or Verdi, the separate designs and testbenches are
reported such that each module, instance, and group from a given version has its own
separate score with data only from the VDB of that version. The top of each separate
design is shown in the Hierarchy pane or report. Modules and covergroups are grouped
by names that start with the specified scope name for each design.

Suppressing Implicitly-Created Coverpoints
As per IEEE 1800-2012 SystemVerilog LRM, ''When a variable V is part of a cross
coverage, SystemVerilog implicitly creates a coverage point for the variable, as if it had
been created by the statement coverpoint V; .'' By default, VCS monitors coverage for
implicitly-created coverpoints to track their cross coverage, which contributes to overall
coverage scores.
Now, VCS provides the flexibility to suppress the reporting of implicitly-created coverpoints
by using either of the following methods:
• The -group suppress_implicit_cps option with the URG
• The covdbSuppressImplicitCPs configuration in UCAPI

When implicit coverpoints are suppressed using either of these methods, they do not
appear in the coverage reports and their coverage is not included in the overall coverage
scores reported.
Consider the following code snippet that shows the covergroup, cg, with a cross of a and
b:
Example 40 Implicitly-Created Coverpoints
reg a, b;
cross a, b;

cg inst = new()
a = 1; b = 1;
inst.sample();
a =0; b = 0;
inst.sample();
end
As a and b are part of the cross, VCS implicitly creates coverpoints for them and treats the
previously highlighted code snippet as follows:
coverpoint a; //implicitly-created coverpoint a
coverpoint b; //implicitly-created coverpoint b
cross a, b;
To suppress the reporting of the implicitly-created coverpoints, a and b, use either of the
following interfaces:
• URG
• UCAPI
URG
URG can be directed to ignore implicitly-created coverpoints using the -group
suppress_implicit_cps option, as shown in the following command:
% urg -dir simv.vdb -group suppress_implicit_cps -format text
When the -group suppress_implicit_cps option is used for Example 40, URG
generates the following report in which coverpoints a and b are not covered for coverage
computation and only the cross a, b is covered:

UCAPI
You might use the following API to suppress scores of implicitly-created coverpoints:
covdb_qualified_configure (designHdl, covdbSuppressImplicitCPs, "true");
Here, the covdbSuppressImplicitCPs configuration is added to the
covdb_qualified_configure interface. When this configuration is set to true,
UCAPI does not calculate coverage scores for implicitly-created coverpoints from the
covdbObjects iterataor list. Also, UCAPI uses the following API to know whether a
coverpoint is implicit:
int isImpl = covdb_get_integer_annotation (ptObj, IS_IMPLICIT_CP);
Displaying Group Ratios For Each Covergroup
By default, URG computes
covergroup
covergroup scores using LRM rules: the score of each
coverpoint
coverpoint and
cross
cross is computed separately, and those scores are averaged to compute
the covergroup's score.
URG allows you to instead compute a
ratio score
ratio score. This scoring method gives a better
estimation of the work left to do to get the covergroup to 100% covered. It works by
counting the total number of covered coverpoint and cross bins in the group, and dividing
that by the total number of coverpoint and cross bins, covered and uncovered. This option
is enabled on the URG command line using the
-group ratio
-group ratio or
-show ratios
-show ratios switch.
URG displays the overall covered and expected ratio for all covergroups in the Total
Groups Coverage Summary table of the Testbench Group List page. For example, if all

covergroups together had 10,000 bins across all of their coverpoints and crosses, and half
were covered, the Testbench Group List page shows a ratio of 5000/10000 in the report.
URG displays the covered and expected count for each covergroup when either the -show
ratios or -group ratio switch is specified on the command line.
To use ratio scoring for covergroups in a report, use either the
-show ratios
-show ratios or
-group ratio
-group
ratio switch on the command line as follows:
urg -dir simv.vdb -show ratios
or
urg -dir simv.vdb -group ratio
If you use the -show ratios switch with URG, URG automatically enables the -group
ratio switch. For details on the -show ratios switch, see the "Displaying Ratio Score in
URG Report" section in the Coverage Technology Reference Manual.
In ratio mode, URG provides two additional columns -
Covered
Covered and
Expected
Expected - in the
Testbench Group List page (see the following figure).
In the figure, the report shows two additional columns, Covered and Expected. The
Covered column displays the count of covered objects in a covergroup. Whereas, the
Expected column displays the count of coverable objects in a covergroup.

Also, the report provides the Hide Ratios link to hide detailed ratio information from the
Group Summary page. If you click the Hide Ratios link, URG shows the following report:
After you hide covergroup ratio details from the page, the Show Ratios link is displayed.
Using this link, you can display the count of covered and coverable ratios whenever
required.
The Covered and Expected columns are added to the URG text report as well (see the
following figure).
Specifying Coverpoint Bins With an Array
The SystemVerilog set_covergroup_expression syntax allows specifying an array
of values that define the bins. This allows you to populate an array to specify values
instead of enumerating them with specific bin expressions. For more details, see Section

19.5.1.2, "Coverpoint bin set Covergroup Expressions" in the IEEE SystemVerilog LRM
Std 1800-2012.
For example, an array of 4 values, arr[4], can be specified as defining the bins for the
cp_bin directive, as follows:
int arr[4];
int x;

covergroup cg(int s[4]);

Support for Embedded Covergroup Inheritance
The coverage score might increase or decrease depending on whether the optimized out
coverage objects are covered or uncovered.
Verdi Integration
The unreachable signals are dimmed in Verdi. The tooltip of an unreachable signal
displays the Unreachable (Optimized) status.
Merging Coverage Reports
When two coverage databases (VDBs) are merged, the coverage reports are generated
as follows:
Base VDB Input VDB Merged Result
Unreachable Covered Unreachable
Unreachable Unreachable Unreachable
Covered Unreachable Reachable
Exclusion Behavior
The optimized signals behave the same way as a signal excluded at compile time. They
cannot be unexcluded, set annotations on, or saved to exclusion files at report time.
Support for Embedded Covergroup Inheritance
This feature allows extending covergroups within SystemVerilog classes, aligning with the
SystemVerilog LRM IEEE Std 1800-2023 specifications. This feature is enabled by default
in VCS.
A derived covergroup might refer to any of the components in its base covergroup. Unless
overridden as shown in the following example, all components belonging to the base
covergroup are also considered belonging to the derived covergroup.

Support for Embedded Covergroup Inheritance
If a derived covergroup has a coverage point with a new name not found in the base
covergroup, it is considered an additional coverage point to be sampled. If a derived
covergroup has a coverage point with a name that is identical to the name of a coverage
point found in its base covergroup, then that coverage point in its base covergroup does
not contribute to the coverage computation.
module top();
class base;
reg a, b;
covergroup cg ;
cp1: coverpoint a;
cp2: coverpoint b;
cr: cross cp1, cp2;
cr2: cross cp1, cp2;
function new();
a = 0; b = 0;
cg = new();
task sample();
cg.sample();
endtask;

class derv extends base;
reg c;
covergroup extends cg;
cp1: coverpoint a; // Overrides the cp1 in base
cp3: coverpoint c;
cr: cross cp1, cp3; // Overrides the cr in base

function new();
super.new();
c = 1;

base bobj = new(); // base class’ object

derv dobj = new(); // derived class’ object

In the preceding example, the coverpoint (cp) and cross (cr) of base covergroup that
have been overridden in the derived covergroup are reported with the additional suffix
overridden<N> to the name. Here, N starts with 1 and is incremented if the same
coverpoint is overridden in multi-level inherited covergroup. The coverpoints and crosses
suffixed with the overridden string do not contribute to the coverage score of the
covergroup and its instances.

text:
Enabling Proper UVM Hierarchical Naming for Covergroup Instances
The reported shape depends on which class instance is created. If the base class object is
created, the base covergroup is reported. If the derived class object is created, the derived
covergroup is reported.
If a derived covergroup specifies a coverage option that is also specified in its base
covergroup, the option in the base covergroup is overridden. If there are coverage options
in the base covergroup that are not overridden, they apply to the derived covergroup.
Enabling Proper UVM Hierarchical Naming for Covergroup
Instances
When working with UVM testbenches in VCS, covergroup instance names sometimes
include internal UVM object names such as me or obj in coverage reports. These names
do not reflect the user-defined verification hierarchy, making it harder to trace coverage
data. This feature ensures that covergroup instance names display the correct UVM
hierarchy (such as uvm_test_top), thereby improving clarity and traceability in coverage
analysis.
To enable this feature, add the -covg_uvm_hier_name compile-time option when
compiling your testbench with VCS. This automatically configures covergroup instance
names to use the UVM hierarchy.
Usage
Two-Step Flow
vcs test.v -full64 -sverilog -ntb_opts uvm -covg_uvm_hier_name
simv
Three-Step Flow
vlogan -sverilog test.v -ntb_opts uvm -full64
vcs top -covg_uvm_hier_name
simv
With this command, VCS compiles your simulation so that coverage results
show covergroup instance names reflecting the full UVM hierarchy, such
as uvm_test_top.env.my_agent.my_covergroup, instead of names like
me.obj.my_covergroup.
If you need full control or backward compatibility between runs with and without this
option, you can explicitly set the instance name from your test class code:
mycg.set_inst_name(this.get_full_name() + ".mycg");

text:
Support for type_option.merge_instances and option.get_inst_coverage
Example Output
When running a test in which a covergroup is embedded in a class derived from
uvm_component, and the top-level testbench instance is named top, the covergroup
instance name in coverage reports appears as:
uvm_test_top.env.scoreboard.mycg
Instead of:
uvm_test_top.env.scoreboard.me.obj.mycg
The following are the limitations of the UVM hierarchical naming for covergroup instances
feature:
• Coverage databases (VDBs) generated with and without -covg_uvm_hier_name
are incompatible for merging unless all instance names are explicitly set using
set_inst_name or option.name.
• Exclusion files and merge operations may fail if instance names do not match because
of specifying this option.
• For covergroups embedded in non-UVM classes but instantiated inside UVM-derived
classes, the full UVM hierarchy is still prepended as per test context.
• This option affects only the naming in reports; functional, compile-time, and runtime
behavior remains unchanged.
Support for type_option.merge_instances and
option.get_inst_coverage
VCS supports two SystemVerilog options, type_option.merge_instances and
option.get_inst_coverage. These options enhance control over type and instance
coverage computations, thereby providing flexibility and precision in coverage analysis.
The following table lists the values and description of the type_option.merge_instances
and option.get_inst_coverage options:
Option Description
type_option.merge_instances This option determines how type coverage is computed. If
the value of the option is set to 1, coverage is calculated
as the union of all instances. If the value of the option is
set to 0, coverage is calculated as the weighted average of
instances.

Support for type_option.merge_instances and option.get_inst_coverage
Option Description
option.get_inst_coverage This option enables the tracking of per-instance coverage. If
the value of the option is set to 1, VCS returns per-instance
coverage through the get_inst_coverage built-in method.
If the value of the option is set to 0, VCS returns the same
value as returned by the get_coverage method.
This option is effective only when the
type_option.merge_instances option is specified.
For more information about the type_option.merge_instances and
option.get_inst_coverage options, refer to the SystemVerilog LRM IEEE Std
1800™-2017.
• Coverage Scores in Report
The type_option.merge_instances and option.get_inst_coverage options are
enabled when they are specified in the covergroup definition. However, if the options
are not specified in the covergroup definition, you must use the -covg_lrm_compliance
compile-time option. With the -covg_lrm_compliance option, the default value of
the type_option.merge_instances option is 0 (weighted average). Without the
-covg_lrm_compliance option, the default value of the type_option.merge_instances
option is 1 (union).
The following is the use model of the -covg_lrm_compliance option:
% vcs -covg_lrm_compliance
In specific scenarios, you must use the -covg_enable_perinst0_options elaboration
option to enable the type_option.merge_instances and option.get_inst_coverage
options. These scenarios are discussed in the following section.
Handling per_instance Setting and Its Impact on Coverage Optimization
The per_instance option controls whether to save the coverage information for the
instance in the coverage database (VDB) and subsequently include in the report. When
the per_instance option is not set, instance-specific data is not saved in the coverage
database. VCS leverages this to optimize memory usage by sharing memory across
all instances of a covergroup variant, rather than maintaining instance-specific data.

Support for type_option.merge_instances and option.get_inst_coverage
However, this optimization prevents retrieval of instance-specific data during simulation.
While it improves read memory (RMEM) and runtime (RT) performance for covergroups,
adjustments are necessary for the following specific scenarios:
• When the per_instance option is set to 0 and the merge_instances option is set to 0.
VCS needs instance-specific data to compute the type coverage of a covergroup
variant using the weighted average of the scores of all instances. However, VCS does
not maintain or dump instance-specific data when the per_instance option is set
to 0. As a result, it disables the memory sharing optimization. In addition, when both
the per_instance and merge_instances options are set to 0, it leads to increased
loading time of VDB, and more memory and disk-space utilization.
• When the per_instance option is set to 0, the merge_instances option is set to 1,
and the get_inst_coverage option is set to 1.
In this scenario, the get_inst_coverage method must report instance-specific
coverage. Instance-specific data is required but not maintained when the
per_instance option is set to 0. It disables optimization conditionally based on
whether the get_inst_coverage method is called for a covergroup instance.
In the preceding scenarios, VCS generates a warning message and ignores the
type_option.merge_instances and option.get_inst_coverage options
unless explicitly overridden. If you want VCS to honor the configurations, use the
-covg_enable_perinst0_options elaboration option.
The following is the use model of the -covg_enable_perinst0_options option:
% vcs -covg_enable_perinst0_options
The -covg_lrm_compliance option enables the
-covg_enable_perinst0_options option. If the -covg_lrm_compliance
is specified in the VCS command line, do not set the
-covg_enable_perinst0_options option.
Coverage Scores in Report
When the type_option.merge_instances option is set to 1, the coverage scores are
computed based on covered bins as follows:

• When the per_instance option is set to 0, the merge_instances option is set to 0,

get disabled. It can lead to runtime performance degradation.
Support for Covergroup Mapping
VCS allows you to map functional covergroups that have same covergroup shapes but
with different hierarchical paths. In addition, VCS allows merging LP covergroups. This
feature enables faster coverage closure and improves verification efficiency.
• Related Notes
To map a functional covergroup from IP to SoC, use the following syntax in the mapping
configuration file:
COVERGROUP: <non-hierarchical covergroup>

Support for Covergroup Mapping
Related Notes
• Embedded covergroups are supported. The following example shows the covergroup
cg is inside the class cls:
module cgmodule();
reg [3:0] a,b;
class cls;
cp1: coverpoint a;
cp2: coverpoint b {
bins b1 = {[0:10]};
}
endgroup;
function new();
cg = new();
function void sample();
cg.sample();
module mid();
cgmodule inst1();
cgmodule inst2();
module tb();
For such covergroup, the mapfile entry is as follows:
COVERGROUP: cls::cg
SRC:blocktb.inst1
DST:tb.m1.inst1, tb.m2.inst1
• Covergroups in $unit package are supported. The covergroup shape name in the
following example is $unit(cls.v)::cg:
cls.v
reg [3:0] a,b;
cp1: coverpoint a;
cp2: coverpoint b {
bins b1 = {[0:10]};
}
endgroup;
module cgmodule();
cg cginst;
cginst = new();
end

Support for Covergroup Mapping
Consider the following where the file name or file path has changed such that the
covergroup shape name is $unit(changedFile.v)::cg:
changedFile.v

reg [3:0] a,b;
cp1: coverpoint a;
cp2: coverpoint b {
bins b1 = {[0:10]};
}
endgroup;
module cgmodule();
cg cginst;
cginst = new();
end
The corresponding mapfile entry is as follows:
COVERGROUP: cg
SRC:$unit(changedFile.v)
DST:$unit(cls.v)
To merge or map the covergroups belonging to different $unit packages,
use the -flex_merge option with drop, union, or reference.
• Covergroups created for LP have a different hierarchical name, PST.group_state. In
addition, the highlighted keyword “#LPGROUP” is needed when the entry corresponds to
LP covergroups. The mapfile entry for LP covergroups is as follows:
COVERGROUP:PST.group_state #LPGROUP
SRC: wave/SAMPLE_wave
DST: tb_top/DUT
• Wildcard “*” is supported in both SRC and DST fields to indicate all instances or
definitions whose name matches the one in the covergroup field is merged. For
COVERGROUP: cginst1
SRC: *
DST: tb.m1.inst1, tb.m1.inst2

COVERGROUP: cginst1
SRC: *

DST: *

COVERGROUP: cg
SRC: blocktb.inst2
DST: *
Covergroup mapping does not support the following:
• Instance-Level mapping of covergroups
• Wildcard, tb.m1.inst1*
• The -map option
• The -group merge_across_scopes option
Test run metrics are non-coverage measurements and records from a simulation run.
For example, test run metrics include elapsed CPU and clock time, number of simulation
cycles, and the maximum amount of memory used. The collective set of these metrics for
a given test run is called its test record.
The following sections discuss how you can write and configure test run metrics:
• Automatically writing test run metrics when coverage is enabled. See section Writing
Test Run Metrics.
• Generating lightweight test records. See section Generating Lightweight Test Records
• Reporting test run metrics using the -show tests option or any -grade option. See
section Reporting Test Run Metrics.
• Configuring reports to control how test run metrics are displayed in the URG tests.txt or
tests.html report. See section Configuring the Reports.
• Writing the test record of a merged database. See section Test Record of a Merged
Database.

Writing Test Run Metrics
Certain test run metrics are written automatically during a simulation run when any type of
coverage is enabled.

This metric data is stored in the same verification database (vdb) directory in which the
runtime coverage data is stored. In addition, it is possible to retain the test run metrics for
the original test runs when merging the VDB data of the original test runs.
This feature is enabled by default; you can disable it during simulation using the
-cm_stats option with the none argument:
% simv -cm_stats none …
Generating Lightweight Test Records
VCS Coverage also provides the option to save test run metrics for a simulation run to a
lightweight VDB directory even when coverage is not enabled. This VDB directory contains
only the test run metrics without any coverage information.
You can create this lightweight VDB by providing the all argument with the -cm_stats
option as follows. This forces the creation of a lightweight VDB directory even when
coverage is not enabled or suppressed:
% simv -cm_stats all
A test record created without coverage data is called a lightweight test record.
A VDB produced by a simulation run when coverage is not enabled contains only the
structure required for storage of the test record and the test record file itself.
You can specify the name of the directory in which the lightweight test record should be
stored using the -cm_dir option as follows:
% simv -cm_stats all -cm_dir mysimv.vdb
The name of the test can be specified on the simv command line by using the -cm_test
option in conjunction with the -cm_name option. Use the -cm_name option to designate a
unique test name under the directory (created using the –cm_dir option) in the VDB to
store the test records. Use the -cm_test option to assign the test an unambiguous name
as shown in the following example:
% simv -cm_stats all -cm_test /rand/usbp/test7 -cm_name test7
The -cm_name option provides the location where the test data needs to be stored. If two
simulations are run with the same -cm_name value, the data of the latest simulation is
overwritten over the first. If you do not provide the -cm_name option, then test is used as a
default. You can then use the –cm_test option to assign a name to your test.
While covergroups enable themselves by default, they can be disabled with the
command line options. You can use the -cm_stats all option in these cases
to force the generation of a test record.

simv command line, even if coverage information is suppressed.
The following figures show the basic rules to generate lightweight test record and to merge
the lightweight test record. You can generate test record-only data into full or standalone
VDBs and both types can be merged with each other.

option, so a test record is generated into a VDB. test2 is also run with coverage and
its results are stored in the same VDB directory. Thus, both lightweight test records and
regular test records coexist in the same VDB directory:

UCAPI covdbAvailableTests Relation
Whether a test record or VDB is lightweight or not, all tests appear in the
covdbAvailableTests relation. They also appear in the output of the urg -show
availabletests option. For example, if the following tests are created:
lightweight.vdb/lightweighttest1
mixed.vdb/lightweighttest2
mixed.vdb/regulartest3
cov.vdb/regulartest4
Every test in every VDB is displayed in the output of the -show availabletests option
as follows:
% urg -dir lightweight.vdb mixed.vdb cov.vdb -show availabletests
Available tests names:
lightweight/lightweighttest1
mixed/lightweighttest2

mixed/regulartest3
cov/regulartest4
Reporting Test Run Metrics
Using the URG -show tests option, or any -grade option automatically displays the
test run metrics for each simulation run. With either of these options, all the test record
information is listed in the tests.html/tests.txt page below the primary list of tests. Each test
record contains
Simtime
Simulation time,
CPUtime
CPU time, start time, finish time, user name, and so on.
In the HTML version, the name of a test in the primary list is linked to its full test record.

Reporting Lightweight Test Records
The rules for reporting lightweight VDBs are shown in the following figures (the rules apply
to both URG and Verdi). You can report/load VDBs containing only lightweight test records
or mixed lightweight and regular VDBs together using the following commands:
urg -dir lightweight.vdb -show tests
or
urg -dir mixed.vdb -dir cov.vdb -grade [grade_type]

Configuring the Reports
Some test run metrics can be displayed in the primary list of tests next to the coverage
scores and test names. This can be used for a quick reference or for sorting the tests
using one of these metrics. Test run metrics are only displayed in the primary list of tests
when the grade option is used. Specify the type of test grading to perform as the sub-
argument to the -grade option (for example, -grade index ), or use -grade list to
create a primary test table without grading the tests.
% urg -dir simv.vdb -grade index list \
columns cputime+clocktime …
This generates a primary list of tests with their CPU times and clock times. The sub-
arguments passed to columns must be separated by the “+” symbol, and include seed,
seed48, simtime, cputime, and clocktime.
Cost-based grading shows the cost type selected for grading and the running total of
that metric, by default. For example, if -grade cost simtime is used, row #N in Table 3
shows the simulation time for test #N along with the simulation time total of the tests 1
through N. You can modify the default behavior and add more columns using the columns
argument.
Example 1
A sample output of the following urg command with -grade list only lists the tests, as
shown in Figure 23. No test metrics are shown as the -grade columns option was not
included.
% urg -dir simv.vdb -grade list

Figure 23 Tests List
Test Record of a Merged Database
While merging the VDBs, the test record information is generated and is available in the
URG report.
For example, execute the following command line to gather the test record information of a
merged database:
% urg -dir simv1.vdb -dir simv2.vdb -dbname merged.vdb -format both
This command gathers the test record from each run in the test.xml file in the merged
database because of the inclusion of the -dbname option.
To dump test records while merging vdbs, it is not required to pass the -show
tests option.
The -show tests option only controls the display of the test records/test correlation data
in the URG reports. You can generate the URG report with the test record of the merged
database using the following command:
% urg -dir merged.vdb -show tests

Discarding Test Records From Merged VDBs
The following are the limitations with this feature:
• Passing the -cm_stats option to the vcs command line with the -R option is not
supported.
• Random seed information is only available when there is covergroup data for the test.
Discarding Test Records From Merged VDBs
VCS enables you to discard those test records that do not cover any objects or cover only
objects that are covered by many other tests when creating a new merged VDB. This
feature guarantees that if test correlation information is saved, every covered object has at
least one test on its list, additionally allowing you to control how the maximum number of
test records to keep per object.
Discarding redundant test records does not have any effect on the coverage scores

least one test on its list, additionally allowing you to control how the maximum number of
test records to keep per object.
Discarding redundant test records does not have any effect on the coverage scores
reported from a merged VDB or whether given objects are marked covered or uncovered.
When a merged VDB is created with test correlation enabled, it trims any test records that
do not appear on at least one coverage object's test correlation list. To enable this feature,
use the -trimtestrecords switch at URG:
urg -show tests -dbname new.vdb [-db_max_tests N] -trimtestrecords

Discarding Test Records From Merged VDBs
where,
• The -show tests switch indicates that test correlation information is saved in the
merged VDB, new.vdb.
• The -db_max_tests option is an optional option that enables you to specify the
maximum number of tests to be saved on the test correlation list of any covered object.
To enable the trim test record feature via UCAPI, set the
covdbTrimTestrecords configuration to anything except NULL or the string
"0".
Consider a design with 5 objects, A, B, C, D, and E. Also, consider that seven tests, t0, t1,
t2, t3, t4, t5, and t6, are loaded such as:
• t0 is the first test on the test list of A, B, and E.
◦ The test correlation data of t0 is A:t0, B:t0, and E:t0.
• t1 is the first test on the test list of C.
◦ The test correlation data of t1 is A:t0, B:t0, C:t1, and E:t0.
• t5 is the first test on the test list of D.
◦ The test correlation data of t5 is A:t0, B:t0, C:t1, D:t5, and E:t0.
• t2 covers only B, t3 and t4 cover only B and C, and t6 covers only E.
◦ The test correlation data of t2, t3, and t4 is A:t0, B:t0, C:t1, and E:t0.
◦ The test correlation data of t6 is A:t0, B:t0, C:t1, D:t5, and E:t0.

Preserving Paths of RTL Source Files
Note that t0, t1, and t5 are kept when the -trimtestrecords switch is used at report
time. If this switch is not used, all test records - t0, t1, t2, t3, t4, t5, and t6 - are stored
in the VDB.
This feature has the following limitations:
• The -show tests switch automatically turns on when -trimtestrecords is used,
otherwise, test correlation details are not saved in the merged VDB. For example:
urg -dir run1.vdb run2.vdb -dbname merged1.vdb -trimtestrecords
This command is equivalent to the following command:
urg -dir run1.vdb run2.vdb -dbname merged1.vdb -trimtestrecords -show
tests
• If the -grade switch is used, -trimtestrecords does not trim any test, as all the tests
should be considered for grading. For example, even when -trimtestrecords is used
in the following command, no test records are discarded as -grade is used:
urg -dir run1.vdb run2.vdb -dbname merged1.vdb -show tests
-trimtestrecords -db_max_tests 3 -grade
Preserving Paths of RTL Source Files
When a coverage-enabled directory or file (simv, simv.daidir, csrc, kdb, or simv.vdb)
is copied from source location to destination, VCS can retain the absolute and relative
paths of RTL source files at the destination location.
To direct VCS to retain paths as their original type (absolute or relative), use the
-preserve_path option at compile time. The syntax of -preserve_path is as follows:,
vcs -sverilog ../test.v -cm tgl -preserve_path
Any path specified, using the -f option or +incdir+ in the vcs command line,
retains their absolute and relative paths when the -preserve_path option is
used at compile time.
The -preserve_path option is used so that if you move or copy one of the compile-time
products, VCS can still find the source files. If you relocate the source files, you can use
the -comdir <pathname> option at report time. VCS provides -comdir <pathname> to

Preserving Paths of RTL Source Files
store the absolute path of the directory into which the source Verilog or VHDL files are
relocated. The syntax of -comdir <pathname> is as follows:
urg -dir simv.vdb -comdir <pathname>
The default value of <pathname> is ./.
The -comdir <pathname> option is implemented in UCAPI as covdbComdir and its
syntax is as follows:
covdb_configure_aux(covdbComdir, "<pathname>"
• URG Report

Elaboration directory: /home/user/comp

vcs -sverilog relativeDir/src/test.v <compile option> -preserve_path
Here, the relative path of test.v is given.
Now, consider that the files are relocated to the following new location: /home/user100/
reloc2
The urg command for this example is as follows:

When the -preserve_path option is given at compile time and -comdir is given at

However, when the -preserve_path option is given at compile time and -comdir is not

The nohierarchy feature allows you to specify a cm_hier file at compile time that specifies

To use this feature, use the following compile-time option:

Score Computation
In the nohierarchy mode, the overall score is computed by combining the numerators and
denominators of all monitored module instances.

The nohierarchy mode has the following limitations:
• Does not support multi-level +tree rules or -module/-tree exclusions.
• URG supports a mode where covergroup scores can be reported in the design
hierarchy. This option (group show_in_design ) is not supported with cm_instr

• Hierarchy information is not present in the coverage database, which is generated from

(default) reporting flows.

Merging Coverage Metrics
Merging is used to analyze the coverage status of your design and testbench across all
simulation runs.
Merging creates a single database of merged data that contains all the coverage
information from your simulation runs.
You can create a merged coverage database by passing the -dbname option to the URG
command line. For example,
% urg -dir simv.vdb -dbname merged_dir/merged_test -format text
This command creates merged_dir.vdb, which contains a single test object named
merged_test. This test contains the merged coverage results from all test runs found in
the simv.vdb directory.
The following command creates merged_dir3.vdb with the default test name test.
% urg -dir simv.vdb -dbname merged_dir3 -format text
If you specify the -show tests option to URG when merging, the resulting merged
database notes, for each covered object, which tests covered it, up to a maximum number
of tests per object. You can also specify the maximum number of tests to be stored for
each object using the -db_max_tests option, as follows:
% urg -dir simv.vdb -dbname merged_dir3 -show tests
-db_max_tests 20
This creates merged_dir3.vdb with a maximum of 20 tests stored for each covered
object. This test correlation data can be shown in generated reports using the -show
tests option. It also plays a role in test grading of the merged VDB. For details on test
grading, see Chapter, Grading Tests for Coverage.
URG provides two methods of merging - Serial and Parallel Merging. You can either
choose serial or parallel merging based on the size and number of the databases, as
described in the following sections:
• Serial Merging
• Parallel Merging

Serial Merging
You can also use the following algorithms to influence how coverage data from different
tests is combined when merging:
• Default merge
• Flexible merge
• Union merge
• Reference merge
Any of these algorithms can be used with either serial or parallel merging. The following
sections describe each algorithm. The choice of algorithm generally affects only
covergroup data, however, reference merging has an impact on assertions data as well.
• Default Merging for Covergroups
• Flexible Merging for Covergroups
• Union Merging for Covergroups
• Reference Merging for Covergroups and Assertions
• Scoped Merging of VDBs
Serial Merging
The default mechanism URG employs to merge test results is serial merging. As the
name implies, this technique merges coverage data of numerous tests one after the other,
serially.
For example, consider that you have run four tests and therefore have four sets of test
results. When you employ serial merging on these tests, it starts merging the test results
of the with the first two tests. It then merges this merged results with the results from the
third test, then merges the new merged results with the results from the fourth test to
generate the final merged test result.
Serial merging is suitable in cases with limited amount of coverage data or fewer number
of test results that need to be merged. In cases with a huge amount of coverage data or
higher number of test results, serial merging might not be a preferable solution as it might
take a considerable amount of time to complete the task.
Parallel Merging
Coverage data can be merged in parallel to significantly speed up processing. With URG’s
parallel merge feature, URG divides the tests to be merged into separate groups. As those

Parallel Merging
groups finish, their results are also combined into parallel jobs, until the final merge is
done.
Coverage offers the parallel merging technique that is suitable in scenarios where there is
a large amount of coverage data that needs to be merged. You can merge coverage data
using parallel merging by specifying the -parallel option on the urg command line.
The urg_parallel.elog file is created if errors occur while using parallel merging. This

amount of coverage data that needs to be merged. You can merge coverage data
using parallel merging by specifying the -parallel option on the urg command line.
The urg_parallel.elog file is created if errors occur while using parallel merging. This
file records errors that occur during one of the sub-processes. If you specify the -verbose
option along with -parallel, the errors and warnings that occur during sub-processes go
to stdout and the following message is generated:
Status: 13 Mergings, 1 remain (12 Done, 0 Running, 1 on queue, 0 waiting)
Merging the Final One
The error messages of sub-jobs are saved in urg_parallel.elog.
Distributed Merging SUCCESSFUL!!!
In parallel merging, a job refers to the process of creating each group.
You can control the number of tests that URG merges into a group, and the number of
lower level groups that go into a higher level merging. If you specify a smaller the number
of tests to be considered per merging, it results in a higher number of jobs (and thereby
levels) created to complete parallel merging.
Specifying the Number of Tests in Merging
You can specify the number of tests that should be considered for merging, and the
number of lower-level mergings in a higher-level merging, using the -parallel_split
integer option, as follows:
urg -dir base.vdb simv1.vdb simv2.vdb -parallel -parallel_split 5
If you specify a lower number of tests per merge, the number of jobs, and the associated
levels increases. Therefore, for twelve tests, specifying a value of 3 creates six jobs on
three levels and specifying a value of 6 creates three jobs on two levels.
You can perform parallel merging using one of the following methods:
• Specifying Hosts to Execute Jobs
• Using a GRID Computing Engine
• Using an LSF Engine

Parallel Merging
Specifying Hosts to Execute Jobs
You can choose the machines on your network that you want to run parallel merging jobs
on. To do so, list the machine names on separate lines in a text file and provide the file
name as an argument to the -parallel option.
The following is an example of a file named machine_file with the machine names listed:
RHEL32_machine1
RHEL32_machine2
RHEL32_machine3
RHEL32_machine4
You can pass machine_file as an argument to the -parallel option as follows:
% urg -dir test0.vdb test1.vdb test2.vdb test3.vdb test4.vdb\ test5.vdb
test6.vdb test7.vdb test8.vdb test9.vdb \ test10.vdb test11.vdb
-parallel machine_file
URG uses the rsh command to run parallel merge jobs on machines specified
this way.
Using a GRID Computing Engine
You can run your parallel merging operation on a GRID computing engine and pass
optional arguments to that engine using the -grid command-line option. You pass the
optional arguments for the engine in quotation marks that follow the option, as shown in
the following example.
Following the -grid option, you can pass the secondary options -sub and -del to run and
clear the GRID engine respectively.
% urg -dir test0.vdb test1.vdb test2.vdb test3.vdb \
test4.vdb test5.vdb test6.vdb test7.vdb test8.vdb \
test9.vdb test10.vdb test11.vdb -parallel -grid \
"-l arch=1x24-amd64 -P bnormal" -sub qsub -del qdel
In this example, URG starts the GRID engine with the qsub command. URG appends -l
arch=1x24-amd64 -P bnormal to the qsub command line. After parallel merging, URG
passes the qdel command to the engine to clear the engine.
Using an LSF Engine
You can also run your parallel merging operation on an LSF engine using the -lsf
command-line option. Similar to the -grid option, you pass the optional arguments to the
engine in quotation marks that follow the option.

With the -lsf option, you must enter the secondary options, -sub and -del, to enter the
commands to create and control jobs in the engine. The following is an example of using
the -lsf option:
% urg -dir test0.vdb test1.vdb test2.vdb test3.vdb \
test4.vdb test5.vdb test6.vdb test7.vdb test8.vdb \
test9.vdb test10.vdb test11.vdb -parallel -lsf \
"-q queuename -R res_req" -sub bsub -del bkill
Using an RTDA Compute Farm
The use of the -rtda urg option with the nc command enables URG parallel merging with
the RTDA Network Computer.
The -rtda urg option, along with the -sub and -del options, is used to set up the
nccommand used in URG parallel merging.
-rtda ["rtda args"] is used to specify RTDA-style merging and RTDA arguments.
Any command other than the nc submit and nc stop commands can be passed as
["rtda args"] .
-sub <submit command> is used to specify submit commands for Grid, LSF or RTDA.
Parallel merging takes the default argument as qsub for Grid, bsub for LSF and nc
submit for RTDA. These default values can be overridden with this argument.
-del <delete command> is used to specify the delete command for Grid, LSF or RTDA.
While the overall algorithm for merging covergroup coverage is the same as for code
coverage, there are some differences and more choices available for covergroup merging.
These differences largely arise from the fact that each simulation run might have a
different set of covergroups in it, and that those groups might have different shapes/
numbers and types of bins due to parameterization. This section discusses the special
merging features that apply only to covergroups.
• Default Merging for Covergroups
• Flexible Merging for Covergroups
• Union Merging for Covergroups
• Reference Merging for Covergroups and Assertions
• Resetting the Scores of all Coverable Objects to Zero

Flexible Merging for Covergroups
This merging technique is available only for covergroup coverage. Flexible merging
enables you to get a more accurate coverage report when the coverage model is still
evolving and you are running tests repeatedly with minor changes in the coverage model
between the test runs. URG facilitates flexible merging using a new merge database
option. It follows a set of rules to merge databases depending on the functional coverage
model.

To enable flexible merging, use the -group flex_merge_drop option on the URG
command line, as follows:
% urg -dir simv1.vdb -dir simv2.vdb -group flex_merge_drop
URG assumes the first specified coverage database as a reference for flexible merging.
Consider two databases, first.vdb and second.vdb. Using the -group
flex_merge_drop option and flexible merging database rules, URG generates a merged
report. For example:
% urg -dir first.vdb -dir second.vdb -group flex_merge_drop
In this example, URG considers the first.vdb coverage database directory as a
reference to generate the flexible merged report.
Merge Equivalence
To merge two coverpoints or crosspoints, you should merge them equivalent to each other.
The following section lists the requirements for merge equivalence.
Merge Equivalence Requirements for Autobin Coverpoints
The coverpoint P1 is said to be merge equivalent to a coverpoint P2 only if the name,
auto_bin_max and the width of the coverpoints are the same, where P1 and P2 are
autobin coverpoints.
Merge Equivalence Requirements for User-Defined Coverpoints
The coverpoint P1 is said to be merge equivalent to a coverpoint P2 only if the
coverpoint names and width are the same.
Merge Equivalence Requirements for Crosspoints
The crosspoint C1 is said to be merge equivalent to a crosspoint C2 , if the crosspoints
have the same number of coverpoints and their corresponding coverpoints are merge
equivalent.
Rules for Flexible Merging of Databases
The following sections list the rules that govern the merging of databases with flexible
merge dropping semantics. By dropping semantics, you can take advantage of the
information available from a newer database to eliminate the redundant information from
the older databases.

Rules for Merging Coverpoints
The coverpoints P(T1) in first test run T1 and P(T2) in the second test run T2 are
merged according to the following rules:
• If the coverpoints are merge equivalent: The merged coverpoints contain a union of all
the coverpoint bins in P(T1) and P(T2), but URG drops the coverpoint bins that are
defined only in the earlier coverage model.
• If the coverpoints are not merge equivalent: The merged coverpoint contains all the
coverpoint bins in the most recent test run and the older test run data is not considered
and dropped.
Rules for Merging Crosspoints
The crosspoint C(T1) in test T1 and C(T2) in test T2 are merged according to the
following rules:
• If the crosspoints are merge equivalent: The merged crosspoints contain a union of all
the crosspoint bins in C(T1) and C(T2), but URG drops the crosspoint bins that are
defined only in the earlier coverage model.
• If the crosspoints are not merge equivalent. The merged crosspoint contains all the
crosspoint bins in the most recent test run and the older test run data is not considered
and dropped.
The example discusses two tests with minor changes in the functional and assertion
coverage models. The changes are marked in boldface.
Example 42 Test01
option.auto_bin_max = 64;
cp2: coverpoint secondsig {
bins first = {[0:63]};
bins mid = {[71:82]};
}
cp3: coverpoint thirdsig;
bit[7:0]signal;
cp4:coverpoint signal;
cc1: cross cp1, cp2;
cc2: cross cp2, cp3 {
bins mybin = binsof(cp2) intersect [0:255];
}
cc3: cross cp2, cp3 {
bins my_st = binsof(cp2) intersect [0:255];
}

merged result and in the reports.
It enables you to gather and merge covergroup data from ongoing simulation runs even as
the coverage model is changing, without losing any data from any version of the model.
The key value is that the coverage gathered for all versions of all parts of a covergroup is
retained, and the data for parts that does not change is merged across all the test runs.
In contrast, reference merge splits covergroups that have any differences between them,
along with their data. Flexible merge is similar to union merge, but flexible merge discards
data from the changed parts of a covergroup, whereas union merge saves the data for
each changed part so that data can be retrieved later if the covergroup definition changes .
Figure 26 illustrates the union merging flow. As simulations run with different models, all
variations are combined to produce a superset coverage model and to merge the merge-
able data down to the coverpoint bin level.
When it is required to generate a snapshot, a specific reference model is chosen and the
superset coverage data is extracted based only on the coverage objects in the union-
merged database that match those in that reference model.
Figure 26 Union Merging for Various Coverage Model Variants

Code coverage is not supported with union merging.
You can perform union merging in URG using the union merge report-time option.
To enable union merging, use the union option along with
-flex_merge
-flex_merge on the urg
command line, as follows:
% urg -dir new.vdb -dir old.vdb -flex_merge union -dbname merge
Rules for Union Merging of Databases
Flexible merging preserves coverage data from coverpoints and crosses that exist in the
latest version of each covergroup. In contrast, union merging preserves all coverpoints
and cross coverage data seen in each covergroup across all simulation runs even as they
change.

order and there is no reference version. Therefore, for a given coverpoint or cross P, the
following rules apply:

Union merging is performed on a covergroup-by-covergroup basis and happens without
splitting a covergroup. For example, all of the following changes are compatible with union
merge:
• New or deleted coverpoints or crosses
• Merge equivalent changes to coverpoints and crosses
• Changes to coverpoints or crosses that make them not merge-equivalent
• Changes to a sampling event
• Changes to the argument list of the covergroup

Therefore, the resulting merged covergroup is not a legal SystemVerilog code (for
example, union merge result might have multiple versions of a single bin, or of a single
coverpoint with the same name). However, the coverage analysis tools and report
generators can still report such groups.
Scoring
Scores are computed normally during union merging. In the default mode, the scores of
each coverpoint and cross are averaged together to compute the score of the group. In
group ratio mode, all numerators (covered count) of coverpoints and crosses are added
and divided by the sum of all denominators (coverable).

A union merged covergroup might contain multiple copies of the same coverpoint or cross.
Scoring treats each of these copies as a separate coverpoint, as if it had a unique name.
Therefore, when a coverpoint is duplicated, both of its scores (or both of its sets of
numerators/denominators) are used to compute the covergroup's score.
Merging
The merging rules described in the section Rules for Union Merging of Databases explain
what happens in union merge mode. This section discusses how other merging modes
handle databases created in union merge mode.
The following are the other merging modes besides union merging:
• Reference merge: This technique merges covergroups with the same name and
shape, but splits covergroups into two copies if the shape (checksum) has changed.
• Flexible merging: This technique also uses a reference database and only discards
data from changed covergroups at a coverpoint and a cross level.
The databases input to reference or flexible merging can be created either by reference,
or flexible, or union merging. The result of a reference merge of two databases splits
covergroups with different shapes; the result of a flexible merge of two databases
eliminates data from non-merge-equivalent covergroup elements.

Changes in the Sampling Event
Changes in the sampling event for a covergroup have no effect on the merged shape
(same as the latest). Therefore, a covergroup with no changes to its coverpoints or
crosses whose sampling event has changed does not have duplicated coverpoints or
crosses.

Reference Merging for Covergroups and Assertions
Reference merging helps you can eliminate the covergroups and assertions/cover
properties that are not present in the latest database (referred as reference/base/latest
database). This merging technique is available only for coverage for covergroups and
assertions. (Code coverage does not allow merging multiple versions of the design.)
Flexible merging of covergroups using the -group flex_merge_drop option enables you
to obtain a merged coverage report when the coverage model is still evolving, and when
you are running tests repeatedly with minor changes in the coverage model between test
runs. Along with the report of the latest database, the covergroups that are not present in
the latest coverage model are also reported.

If there are multiple tests present in the base database, URG selects one of those tests
as the base test and it would be considered as the reference test. URG does not specify
which test would be considered as the base test. Therefore, it is always recommended
to pass a base database containing only the test that contains the entire and the latest
coverage model.

Consider that the latest coverage model has covergroups CG1, CG2, CG3, but different
seeds lead to instantiation of different covergroups in each test, as follows:
latest.vdb/test1: CG1, CG2
latest.vdb/test2: CG2
latest.vdb/test3: CG1, CG3
latest.vdb/test4: CG1, CG2, CG3 // contains the whole coverage model
old.vdb/test: CG1, CG3, CG4, CG5
In this case, urg -dir latest.vdb -dir old.vdb -flex_merge reference selects
one of the tests in latest.vdb as the base test and the remaining tests are considered
as old tests. Depending on which test is selected as the base test, the results of
-flex_merge reference change as follows:
• If the base test is latest.vdb/test1, the result is:
CG1 // Cumulative of reset.vdb/test1,test3,test4, old.vdb/test
CG2 // Cumulative of reset.vdb/test1,test2,test4
• If the base test is latest.vdb/test2, the result is:
CG2 // Cumulative of reset.vdb/test2,test1,test4
• If the base test is latest.vdb/test3, the result is:
CG1 // Cumulative of reset.vdb/test3,test1,test4, old.vdb/test
CG3 // Cumulative of reset.vdb/test3,test4, old.vdb/test
• If the base test is latest.vdb/test4, the result is:
CG1 // Cumulative of reset.vdb/test4,test1,test3, old.vdb/test
CG2 // Cumulative of reset.vdb/test4,test1,test2
CG3 // Cumulative of reset.vdb/test3,test4, old.vdb/test
In these results, test4 yields the expected results with respect to the latest coverage
model. Therefore, it is recommended to pass a database containing only test4 (a test that
contains the entire coverage model) as the base database to obtain correct results.

Union Merge of Modules
Merging combines coverage from multiple databases to produce a unified database that
contains their combined results. VCS reports coverage for each instance of each module.
It also reports merged coverage for all instances of each module that have the same
shape (that is, for each variant of the module).
If all of the databases are created from the same version of the design, each module
and instance have the same shape and the coverage is merged. While merging code
coverage across multiple configurations of the design, the objects and instances in the
base configuration are used as a reference. By default, the data for an instance in an
input database that does not exist in the base database is ignored, and its contribution to
the overall coverage score of its module is lost. In previous VCS versions, it was already
possible to collect the coverage for a specific list of modules across different design
configurations using the -map and -mapfile options. However, -map and -mapfile cannot
handle the scenario where there is no VDB containing the superset of all modules that
is used as the base VDB. The new -flex_merge modules option to URG provides the
ability to merge modules even if there is no single VDB that contains all modules. When
this option is given, URG automatically merges the code coverage for each variant of
each module that appears in any of the specified databases. The instance-level coverage
data is still reported separately, but the module-level coverage data takes data from all
configurations.
Note that module-level data is only merged when the module's coverage shape is the
same (that is, they are from the same variant of the module). For example, the data for all
instances of a 16-bit adder across different design configurations is merged together, but
the data for any 32-bit versions of the same adder is kept separate.

Unlike in the default mode, the order of databases passed to URG does not change

different. For example, the following commands result in identical scores:

This feature has the following limitations:
• Test grading cannot be done when creating a report using -flex_merge modules .
You can create a merged VDB using -flex_merge modules and run test grading on it.
However, test grading works on the design hierarchy, not the modules, so each design
hierarchy (configuration) is treated as an independent set of coverable objects for test
grading.

• Modules in different libraries are treated as different entities and therefore, they are not
merged across design hierarchies.
• If a design is compiled with -cm_seqnoconst or -cm_noconst, coverable objects (such
as line, condition, branch, and toggle coverage targets) that are not reachable in that
configuration are marked unreachable. After -flex_merge modules , an object is
reported as UNREACHABLE only if it is marked unreachable in all the input VDBs.
If the object is reachable in at least one input VDB, it is reported as reachable in the
merged result.
The scoped merging feature enables a new type of VDB directory called a VDB Merged
Directory (VDM), where the design and testbench coverage from different VDBs is kept
strictly separate. A report generated from a VDM directory shows separate hierarchies and
separate sets of function coverage data for each design version.
Unlike regular merging where coverage from different VDBs is combined by name and
shape into a single unified result, scoped merging preserves the identity of each design
version. The VDBs of the original versions exist side-by-side in the result, each identified
by a unique scope name prefix.
A VDM can have additional design versions added to it incrementally. Each version in
the VDM has a unique name prefix used to distinguish it in reports and in Verdi coverage
sessions. These names can also be used to refer to different versions from inside an HVP
Verification Plan.

Command Line Usage
To create a VDM with URG, use the -flex_merge separate option. In this mode,
specify the scope name to use for each design version using the ## syntax after the
corresponding VDB name:
% urg -dir version1.vdb##v1 version2.vdb##v2 \
-dbname sepmerge12 -flex_merge separate
Additional VDBs can be added to an existing VDM:
% urg -dir sepmerge12.vdb version3.vdb##v3 \
-dbname sepmerge123 -flex_merge separate
The VDBs passed to -dir must be merged VDBs containing a single test only. Each VDB
passed to -dir must have a unique scope name specified using the ## syntax.
If a scope name is not provided, the following error is issued:
% urg -dir version1.vdb version2.vdb \
-dbname sepmerge12 -flex_merge separate

Error-[UCAPI-MSTN] Missing top name for separated merge
VDB version1.vdb was passed to -dir in flex_merge separate mode
without a top name specified.
In flex_merge separate mode a unique top name must be given for
each VDB. For example: urg -dir simv.vdb##v1
If only one VDB is passed to -dir, a new VDB is created with the specified scope name
added:
% urg -dir version4.vdb##v4 -dbname sepmerge4 -flex_merge separate
Two VDMs with unique scope names can be combined:
% urg -dir sepmerge12.vdb sepmerge34.vdb \
-dbname sepmerge1234 -flex_merge separate

The -flex_merge separate option must be specified if any input VDB is a
VDM.
Two VDMs can only be combined if all their scope names are unique. If duplicate scope
names are detected, the following error is issued:
% urg -dir sepmerge12.vdb sepmerge13.vdb \
-dbname sepmerge123 -flex_merge separate

Error-[UCAPI-SMX] Duplicate top names in separated merge
The VDMs sepmerge12.vdb and sepmerge13.vdb both contain data
with top name "v2". VDMs can only be combined when all top
names are unique.
Merging Restrictions
Any type of merged VDB may be merged as a separate VDB using -flex_merge
separate, regardless of whether it was created with default merging, -map/-mapfile, or
one of the other -flex_merge options.
However, once a VDB is merged into a VDM, its coverage can no longer be merged with
any other VDBs in any way, except to add more VDBs in other scope names to the VDM
itself. This includes any kind of default, -flex_merge, or -map/-mapfile type operation.
The VDM is intended as the last step to take before generating a report. If more data must
be added to a VDB that is going to be reported from a VDM, all of the new data should be
merged with the regular VDB first, and then a new VDM should be created.
Exclusions
Exclusions created using a VDM include scope names. As a result, those exclude files
cannot be later used on a regular VDB as it will not contain the scope name.

Exclusions
Exclusions created using a VDM include scope names. As a result, those exclude files
cannot be later used on a regular VDB as it will not contain the scope name.
For example, an instance dut.chk1 under a scope name V1 would have an .el file entry
like this:
CHECKSUM: "1017343997 2493925923"
INSTANCE: ##v1.dut.chk1
Similarly, hier files specified at report time must include scope names (or wildcards) to
be used on a VDM. For example, a -hier file entry for the above instance could use this
syntax:
-tree ##v1.dut.chk1
To make entries scope-name neutral, use a wildcard:
-tree *dut.chk1

This does not apply to compile-time hier files (-cm_hier, -cm_assert_hier)
because separated scope names can only exist in a VDB, not in any design.

separate score with data only from the VDB of that version. The top of each separate
design is shown in the Hierarchy pane or report. Modules and covergroups are grouped
by names that start with the specified scope name for each design.

Objects in $unit Scope
Coverable objects that are declared outside of any module are reported in the $unit
scope in their compile unit. The scope names are prefixed before their $unit names. For
ASSERTIONS CATEGORY SEVERITY ATTEMPTS REAL SUCCESSES
FAILURES INCOMPLETE
##v2.\$unit::foo.v .glb 0 0 0 0
0 0
Tests
A simulation VDB contains one or more tests, and their names are a combination of the
VDB name and the name given on the simv command line with -cm_name. For example, a
VDB named simv1 could contain tests simv1/test1, simv1/test2, and so on.
A VDB created through normal merging contains a single test, which is named test by
default, and its name is shown in reports as, for example, merge1/test.
When VDBs are merged into a VDM, the names of the tests they contain are given the
same prefix used for the hierarchy, module names, and covergroups. For example, after
a separated merge, the resulting VDM could contain tests named ##v1.simv1/test1,
##v1.simv1/test2, or ##v2.merge1/test.
Because only VDBs containing exactly one test can be combined in a VDM, there is only
one test per scope name in the VDM result.

Planner Annotation
Because each design in a VDM has a unique scope name, HVP plans can use that name
to indicate which version of an instance, module, or covergroup to use as a source.
For example, to refer to covergroup scores from the group top.mm1::grp1 in a separated
design named V2, the syntax would be:
feature F1;
measure Group g1;
source = "##v2.top.mm1::grp1";
If the plan or feature hierarchy is meant to be shared across multiple design versions,
parameters can be used so that when the plan or feature is instantiated, it can include an
argument specifying which scope name to use.
If the feature is meant to refer to a source in all of the separate designs, a wildcard can be
used instead of the scope name in the source string.
The Scoped Merging of VDB feature has the following limitations:
• A VDM can only be combined with additional design versions by adding new scope
names. No object-level coverage merging can be done on a VDM.
• A scope name for a VDB may only be added by using -flex_merge separate along
with the ## syntax on the URG command line. Scope names cannot be specified at
runtime, and scope names inside of VDMs cannot be changed.
In general, coverage data collected for a module in a simulation run can only be merged
with a compile-time VDB directory that was compiled with the same version of the module
that was used in the simulation run. When merging, if the coverage data for a module or
instance produced by simulation does not match what is found in the compiled VDB, the
data from that simulation run is discarded.
This section describes a feature that allows coverage data for toggle coverage to be
merged on a signal-by-signal basis instead of module-by-module (or instance-by-instance)
basis under a switch.

When toggle coverage reference merging is enabled, coverage data for signals that exist
in the input design but do not exist in the base design, or which have different bounds
or types in the base and input design, are discarded and a mismatch report can be
generated.
The base design is the first design and the input design is the other design to be merged
with the base design. If there are multiple input designs, each design is merged one at a
time with the base design.
To enable reference toggle coverage merging, use the -flex_merge tgl switch with the
urg command. Its syntax is as follows:
% urg -dir < base.vdb> < input.vdb> -flex_merge tgl

where,
• <base.vdb> and <input.vdb> are the base database and input database respectively.
Note that both directories must be either a compile-time VDB or a merged VDB
produced with URG's -dbname option. VDBs that are produced using the -cm_dir
option on the simv command line cannot be merged in this mode.
• -flex_merge tgl enables reference merging for toggle coverage metric.
The rules for toggle reference merging are as follows:
1. Only signals that exist in the base design are retained. Signals that exist only in the
input design are discarded.
2. Coverage data of the signals that exist in both databases with same bounds and size
are merged from both designs.
3. For a signal that exists in both databases but has different bounds, only the data from
the base design for that signal is retained.
4. For a signal that exists in both databases but has a different type, only the data from
the base design for that signal is retained.

To use reference merging with coverage data, VDBs should contain design and shape
information as well as runtime coverage data. This information is required to match the

Therefore, toggle coverage merging is supported on compile-time VDBs or merged VDBs.
Toggle coverage merging does not support simulation-only VDBs.
Stricter Shape Checks for Merging
When a code coverage metric is applied to a module instance in a design, it creates a
shape for that metric-module instance pair. All of the instances of a module that have the
same shape for a given metric are tracked as a single variant of the module.

Stricter Shape Checks for Merging
When coverage is merged from two databases, VCS verifies that the shape of a given
variant in the base design database matches the shape for the variant of the same name
in the input database. If the shapes of a metric for a given variant are the same in both
databases, VCS merges the coverage for that metric, for that variant of the module.
Note that no additional switch is required to enable this feature.
This section consists of the following sections:
• Computing and Enabling Stricter Shape Checks
• Migrating Exclusion Files
Computing and Enabling Stricter Shape Checks
To compute stricter shape checks for any coverage metric, use the following command:
vcs -sverilog test.v -cm line -cm_dir <base.vdb/input.vdb>
First, compile the design and then enable stricter shape checks at report time by providing
the -merge_strict switch on the URG command line as follows:
urg -dir base.vdb input.vdb -merge_strict
Migrating Exclusion Files
Exclusion checksums can change from the previous release. To turnoff the functionality of
-cm_instr strict_check , use -cm_instr nostrict .
To migrate exclusion files, perform the following steps:
1. Load a database generated from a compiled design and an existing exclude file into
Verdi using the following command:
verdi -cov -covdir <base.vdb/input.vdb> -elfile
<existing_exclude_file> -excl_bypass_checks
2. Save all exclusions in a new exclude file using File --> Save all exclusions. The Save
All Exclusions for Design dialog box appears (see Figure 30).

Coverage Merging Across Different Libraries
VCS enables you to merge coverage of modules across different libraries for all coverage
metrics using the -merge_across_libs switch. The syntax of the -merge_across_libs
switch is as follows:
urg -dir <base.vdb> -dir <input.vdb> -merge_across_libs
• Reusing Exclusions Using -merge_across_libs
• URG Report

Reusing Exclusions Using -merge_across_libs
When an exclusion file is generated without -merge_across_libs, the names of
coverable objects in the file include library information, for example:
For a module excluded for code coverage: \LIB1.mod
For an excluded covergroup: \LIB1.CG
Exclusion files created without the -merge_across_libs switch do not work as expected
when loaded with VDBs created using -merge_across_libs, because the covergroup
names that include library names do not match the names in the merged VDB. If you
load an exclusion file created without -merge_across_libs for a VDB created with
-merge_across_libs, warnings such as those shown in the following example are
printed:

Setting the SNPS_COVERAGE_DONT_CARE_LIB environment variable to 1 matches exclusion
objects containing library prefixes to coverage objects in a database generated using
-merge_across_libs that does not contain library information.

cov_unit1 from both base and input VDBs is reported with the names as follows:
INPUT.pkg::cov_unit1 BASE.pkg::cov_unit1
Note that the library name BASE or INPUT is prepended to pkg::cov_unit1 when

If -merge_across_libs and -flex merge union are used at URG, then the coverage
